lxc_4fad4e0dae3ceb20.text: Many language cafés split the time in half.

lxc_43c0292e205f5698.text: This way, both people get the same time to learn.

lxc_fc3580261dbfc32e.text: This way, you meet many people quickly.

lxc_c06d345a50ac5e92.text: You talk with one person for 3 minutes.

lxc_7ddd54dc319fa5c3.text: But how do you find the right person in a busy room?

lxc_1fe0aa4ab8cb244d.text: Then you move to the next person.

lxc_0321536bb8ad6115.text: You ask the host: Are the snacks included?

lxc_6a31fce7bfadc615.text: Koffie verkeerd has more milk than coffee, so it is the wrong way around.

lxc_c8ecc9c2d06a0e7b.text: If you are hungry, you ask the waiter: What is an empanada?

lxc_7f28d1acc2be5c41.text: At the Dutch Language Café, the Thursday ticket costs €11.

lxc_28572ee0a8694d60.text: On the menu, you see a funny name: koffie verkeerd.

lxc_1c2c23a32d4b5def.text: In English, koffie verkeerd is wrong coffee.

lxc_ca65742304e271b7.text: At the bar, you order: Can I have a koffie verkeerd, please?

lxc_058f02fba1dda081.text: Then you ask: How much is it?

lxc_1457bcd0ea33e69e.text: It is a small pastry, with cheese, meat or vegetables inside.

lxc_5c0df80ce7be4617.text: A normal Dutch coffee has only a little milk.

lxc_cf2af2a0d78e4780.text: The ticket pays for snacks and games.

lxc_2d09d7a09bacfe1d.text: The snacks are things like popcorn and nuts.

lxc_9d45f91ddced84ec.text: But drinks are not in the ticket, so you buy them at the bar.

lxc_28ef28df1dc5ce5c.text: Then you say: Nice to meet you.

lxc_eb73c8843a1754ae.text: At the same time, they say their name: Hi!

lxc_7e21ca9b63e27974.text: Then Lucía asks: What about you?

lxc_37a2b694e0255af4.text: In the Netherlands, people shake hands when they meet someone new.

lxc_85e18b305e1971b1.text: In a 3-minute speed exchange, you do not have much time.

lxc_0186e55ae933f28d.text: The first time you meet a Dutch person, do not ask: How are you?

lxc_9a7864ec6f66bf1f.text: It gives people a question to ask, for example: Where do you work?

lxc_158c0f772b92554f.text: In Japan, many people bow, or bend forward, and say their family name.

lxc_8d13b3af654e3b7e.text: Often they say only their first name.

lxc_fa3360ed24050a27.text: I study Dutch because I work in The Hague.

lxc_92cc795b9e36a4a9.text: So say three things: your name, your city and why you study the language.

lxc_239fabaacb9138b6.text: Many Dutch people use this question only with people they already know.

lxc_25479e8d59b2e679.text: A stranger is a person you do not know.

lxc_9d0b71e142fa9244.text: If a stranger asks this, a Dutch person may think you met before.

lxc_829977b9f83b6c04.text: But for Dutch people, a hello without a name is rude, or not polite.

lxc_79b676b369051b7c.text: Dutch people like to be clear, so they start with a name.

lxc_e0b74b95082ef217.text: They may think they forgot you!

lxc_df4f07d828e76de9.text: The last part is the most useful.

lxc_af8ef6119f9d3b02.text: When you hear a new name, you say your name too.

lxc_ca9d5be49d18ee8c.text: You ask about time: How long have you lived here?

lxc_4d98c296e60973bc.text: So say thank you with kind words: It was nice to talk to you.

lxc_9d42a6c14fcab8c0.text: You ask about her city: What is Valencia like?

lxc_8896722b0cdff6fe.text: Follow-up questions worked best of all.

lxc_f878fb0b77656db0.text: The best tool for a long conversation is the follow-up question.

lxc_8e49566cd88581e0.text: A follow-up question stays with her idea: What do you do at the hotel?

lxc_2fb285e280d65b22.text: Each follow-up question uses one part of what she says.

lxc_35e8758968283b24.text: A follow-up question shows that you are really listening.

lxc_4dc3f50d05ebb25f.text: In 2017, scientists at Harvard University studied how strangers talk.

lxc_a8969a66b0f25090.text: This is a question about what the other person just said.

lxc_8af728850edc7817.text: The other person gave you their time.

lxc_d5700b61718f86dc.text: When you want to leave, end the conversation in a kind way.

lxc_63a75ea32b2df901.text: People who asked more questions were liked more by their partners.

lxc_b89e2620baadbb0e.text: A new question jumps to a new idea: Do you like football?

lxc_b3b637f84eb9fa27.text: Lucía also says: I moved here from Valencia.

lxc_531732b196593552.text: You ask about her reason: Really?

lxc_f03616b1082c6c54.text: Lucía says: I work at a hotel.

lxc_e2c38dd53c315229.text: You arrive at the Dutch Language Café, Herengracht 13A, in The Hague.

lxc_c82dcb5afb6f2e4e.text: You signed up online, and your ticket was €11.

lxc_84e58c3f3d6dcbf5.text: Your goal: get your sticker, then order a drink and some food.

lxc_e3ce10d3517bed87.text: A host says hello to you.

lxc_894430d8dd088118.text: Your goal: shake hands, say your name and learn something about her.

lxc_dd63f65f637ed0a4.text: You sit down at a table with your coffee.

lxc_72883b9fe2ff3794.text: Her sticker shows Dutch, English and Spanish.

lxc_7dcde20e2b712b28.text: A Dutch woman sits next to you.

lxc_0b6d6975aac1ec22.text: You and your partner take turns choosing the language.

lxc_3a85720eb8487a90.text: Your goal: practise English first, then help Daan with his Japanese.

lxc_4ec9bfad3ffddaf4.text: His sticker shows Dutch, English and a little Japanese.

lxc_b0c6e8b1bd82d79e.text: You talk with each person for 3 minutes.

lxc_05e09dc2603eb6b8.text: Your goal: ask follow-up questions, then end the conversation in a kind way.

lxc_b085b1ad9a7f525a.text: It is 20:30, and you sit at the English table.

lxc_2b090369d7a0fbcc.text: Sanne is there, and you meet Lucía from Spain.

lxc_6c6c4c00a448205f.text: Ask at least three follow-up questions.

lxc_a1000f2c3e15a42f.text: Practise the evening at the Dutch Language Café again.

lxc_b8b6bcc635834630.text: The other person plays the host, the waiter, Sanne, Daan and Lucía.

lxc_b7703653687e77c5.text: Get your sticker, and order a koffie verkeerd and a cheese empanada for €10.50.

lxc_2284f4d089622ca9.text: Shake hands, and say your name, your city and why you study English.

lxc_2c9a49e5c5fa83d2.text: One of you is the visitor.

lxc_d78c8a65dce62ec1.text: Then change roles and use your real life.
